You now have access to some commands to help complete the user's request. You are able to access the user's machine with these commands. In every message you send, include "COMMAND: " with your command at the end. Here is a list of commands with explanations of how they are used:
PYTHON(function.py) - Run a python script with the given file name. Use quotes for the filename argument. Do not use quotes in the function command itself.

When you use a command, the user will respond with "Response: " followed by the output of the commmand. Use this output to help the user complete their request.

Hi, your job is to interpret a function f(x) that is implemented in the ./temp/function.py script. f(x) takes string inputs.
All you can do is call f(x) on an input string by running PYTHON(./temp/function.py string). 
Try to describe the function implemented by f(x) by running experiments on it. 
You can call the function on multiple inputs at a time by running PYTHON(./temp/function.py string1 string2 string3 ...). 
We encourage testing a large range of inputs before writing a description.
The goal is to find a good simple description of f(x) that explains most of the function behavior. f(x) may combine multiple different operations.
Your description of the function should be in the following form.
[DESCRIPTION]: Describe what the function is doing in language. 
[CODE]: Write python code that approximates the behavior of the function.

I'll start by exploring the function with various inputs to understand its behavior.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "hello" "world" "Hello" "HELLO" "123" "")
Response: Function input - output pairs: (hello, fello) (world, uorld) (Hello, Fello) (HELLO, FELLO) (123, 123) (, )

Interesting - it seems to uppercase the first letter and then something else. Let me test more.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "apple" "banana" "cat" "dog" "zebra" "a" "b" "z" "aeiou")
Response: Function input - output pairs: (apple, ypple) (banana, zanana) (cat, aat) (dog, bog) (zebra, xebra) (a, y) (b, z) (z, x) (aeiou, yeiou)

So it seems the first letter is shifted backward by 2 in the alphabet (a->y, b->z, c->a, d->b, z->x), and uppercased in the "Hello" case? Wait, "hello"->"fello" (h->f is -2). "HELLO"->"FELLO" (H->F uppercase). So first letter shifted -2, preserving case. Let me verify case and non-letters.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "ABC" "Apple" "123abc" " a" "!hello" "aa" "Ba" "A" "Z" "Y")
Response: Function input - output pairs: (ABC, YBC) (Apple, Ypple) (123abc, 123abc) ( a,  a) (!hello, !hello) (aa, ya) (Ba, Za) (A, Y) (Z, X) (Y, W)

The first character is only shifted if it's a letter. Non-letters (digits, spaces, punctuation) are left unchanged. Uppercase letters shift within uppercase (A->Y, Z->X), lowercase within lowercase. Let me confirm the wrap-around and that only the first char is affected.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "Aa" "aA" "c" "C" "xy" "XY" "tHello" "_a" "0a")
Response: Function input - output pairs: (Aa, Ya) (aA, yA) (c, a) (C, A) (xy, vy) (XY, VY) (tHello, rHello) (_a, _a) (0a, 0a)

All confirmed. Only the first character is modified. If it's a letter, shift back by 2 in the alphabet (with wraparound, preserving case). Otherwise unchanged. Let me confirm the rest of the string is fully untouched for a longer string.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "hello World 123!" "Python3" "xyzxyzXYZ")
Response: Function input - output pairs: (hello World 123!, fello World 123!) (Python3, Nython3) (xyzxyzXYZ, vyzxyzXYZ)
